text_blocks.snippet: Android Runtime (ART) is the virtual machine that runs apps and some system services on Android devices. ART works by:

list.title: Compiling code ahead of time
list.snippet: ART uses Ahead of Time (AOT) compilation to compile code before the app is executed. This is different from Dalvik, the previous virtual machine, which used Just In Time (JIT) compilation. AOT compilation makes the machine code ready before the app runs, which significantly improves runtime performance.

list.title: Generating a profile
list.snippet: When an app is first run, ART interprets methods that aren't AOT-compiled. It then generates a local profile based on how the app is executed. If the app was installed with a dex metadata file, ART combines the local profile with the cloud profile.

list.title: Recompiling the app
list.snippet: When the device is idle and charging, a compilation daemon re-compiles the app based on the profile generated during the first few runs.

text_blocks.snippet: ART has been the default virtual machine for Android since Android 5.0 (Lollipop). However, some older devices may still use Dalvik if they haven't been updated to a newer version of Android.
